sections.title: Geography
sections.text: Cairo lies on the Nile, just south of where the river fans out into its delta. Greater Cairo is one of the largest urban areas in Africa and the Arab world. The climate is desert: hot, sunny and almost rainless. The Giza pyramids stand where the green river valley meets the Western Desert.

sections.title: History
sections.text: People have lived here for thousands of years. Ancient Memphis, Egypt's first capital, lies a little to the south. The Fatimid dynasty founded al-Qāhira, "the Victorious", in 969 CE, next to the older town of Fustat. Medieval Cairo grew into a great centre of Islamic learning and trade, and its historic core is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sections.title: Culture
sections.text: Cairo is loud, warm and sociable. Neighbourhood coffeehouses (ahwa) stay busy late into the night, the Khan el-Khalili bazaar has traded since the 14th century, and the call to prayer rings out from hundreds of minarets five times a day. Egyptians are known for their humour and their hospitality towards guests.

etiquette: Dress modestly. Women should bring a scarf to cover their hair in mosques.
Use your right hand to eat, and to give or receive things.
During Ramadan, don't eat, drink or smoke in public during daylight hours.
Bargaining is expected in markets. Keep it friendly and smile.

planned.name: Khan el-Khalili
planned.blurb: A bazaar of narrow lanes, lanterns and spice stalls, founded in 1382.

timeline.text: Pharaoh Khufu's Great Pyramid is completed at Giza, near Egypt's royal city of Memphis.
Khafre builds the second pyramid, and the Great Sphinx is carved from the rock.
Alexander the Great conquers Egypt. Greek-speaking kings, the Ptolemies, will rule for three centuries.
Egypt becomes a province of Rome. A Roman fortress, Babylon, guards the Nile crossing here.
Arab armies conquer Egypt and found the city of Fustat beside the Roman fortress.
The Fatimid dynasty founds al-Qāhira, "the Victorious": Cairo.
Saladin begins building the great Citadel on the Muqattam hills.
The Khan el-Khalili bazaar is founded in the heart of the medieval city.
The Ottoman Empire conquers Egypt, and Cairo becomes a provincial capital.
Napoleon's army and scholars arrive and survey the pyramids.
Khedive Ismail comes to power and begins to rebuild Cairo with Parisian-style boulevards.
The Suez Canal opens, and Cairo celebrates with grand festivities.
The Arab League is founded in Cairo.
Millions fill the streets of Cairo for the funeral of President Nasser.
The first line of the Cairo Metro opens, the first in Africa.
Greater Cairo is home to over twenty million people, and the new Grand Egyptian Museum stands near the pyramids.
